target_customer: Tenants and landlords in Latin America who pay or collect monthly rent (originally homeowners wanting to buy before selling, under the Acasa name)
problem: Rent is a household's largest monthly expense yet earns no rewards or credit history in Latin America. Before the pivot the stated problem was buying a new home before the old one sells.
business_model: Rent payment platform with fees and rewards, earlier a bridge financing product funded by debt
product_category: Proptech and consumer fintech rent payments

founders.name: Mauricio Peñaranda
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. Later YC page version reportedly lists him under former founders.

founders.name: Nicolas Penaranda
previous_startups: Ag-tech startup for small farmers in Colombia (failed after 18 months)
Healthy snacks consumer business (partly sold to an FMCG company during COVID)
founders.background_notes: Over 5 years of management consulting in banking and insurance per YC page. Role COO per Bloomberg Linea.

founders.name: Eduardo Restrepo
founders.background_notes: 13+ years in corporate finance including 6 as CFO, employers not named on the YC page.

exit.reason: Not stated by the company. PitchBook lists the company as out of business with a liquidation deal type (seen only in a search result summary).

competitors.name: Habi
competitors.what: Colombian proptech that buys homes directly, named by Bloomberg Linea as the other Colombian proptech operating in Mexico; competes with the original Acasa buy-before-sell model, not the later rent product
competitors.traction_then: Began operations in Mexico late in Q3 2021

competitors.name: Arrenda
competitors.what: Mexican fintech offering advance rent and credit to landlords; adjacent to the rent payments market
competitors.traction_then: Pre-launch at the time of reporting
competitors.funding_then: US$26.5M pre-seed of equity and debt led by Fasanara Capital

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments aggregation, credit reporting and rewards integrations are standard engineering. The earlier bridge loan model needed credit underwriting and a debt facility rather than hard technology.

defensibility.rationale: Rent payment rewards can be copied by banks or payment fintechs; the only edge would be landlord and tenant network density and debt access.

incumbents: Latin American banks and card issuers
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move is documented in the sources read.

market_need_then: Rent is the largest monthly household expense with no rewards or credit building in Latin America. The earlier model addressed the difficulty of buying a home before selling the current one, a need stated in 2022 coverage.

identity.voice_and_tone: Consumer rewards positioning on the YC page

rebrands.why: Search coverage links the rename to the pivot from home bridge financing to rent payments; no company statement on the name was found

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, mascot or community was found. The rename left Acasa press under a different name, and a separate London company also used Acasa.

pivots.from: Acasa: buy before you sell bridge financing for homeowners
pivots.to: Castia: rent payment platform with rewards and credit building
pivots.why: Search coverage quotes co-founder Eduardo Restrepo citing inflation, higher interest and mortgage rates and weaker venture capital interest; the old model was described as in the freezer

outcome_analysis: Acasa raised a US$4.7M seed and US$33M of debt in March 2022 to fund bridge loans, then pivoted within months to rent payments as rates and funding conditions turned. YC lists Castia as inactive and PitchBook shows liquidation, but no founder statement or news report explaining the final cause was found, so the cause is not public beyond the macro driven pivot.
notes: Company site www.castia.com returned HTTP 503 on fetch, so its state is unknown. The pre-seed of about US$1.1M rests on one Forbes Colombia headline seen in search results; its date is unknown and Bloomberg Linea says Wollef led a prior round. CB Insights shows US$38.42M over 5 rounds, matching the March 2022 total only in part. Pivot reason and PitchBook liquidation were read from search result summaries, not opened pages. Nicolas Peñaranda role from Bloomberg Linea.
